# Notix
English | 中文
Desktop notifications for DeepSeek Harness — native **macOS** and **Windows** notifications when the
agent **needs your input**, **runs too long**, **fails**, or **finishes**. One package, no separate
UI package, no approval logic, no agent blocking.
Notix is a pure observer: it never registers an approval/answerer, never appends session events, and
never blocks the agent loop. It watches the shared event surfaces and delivers notifications throug
h a pluggable channel registry with built-in macOS and Windows system channels.
> **Status:** `v0.3.0` — first public release, on the npm registry. macOS and Windows are supported.

>
> **Install:** `dsh plugin --profile <name> add notix-dsh` (see Install), or use the repo-clone i
nstall to run a checkout.

## Why Notix
- **One package, both halves.** The Host plugin and the Plugins settings UI ship in one npm package,

so there is no second `notix-dsh-ui` to install and keep in sync.
- **A pure observer.** Notix neve
r answers approvals, never writes session events and never blocks the agent; delivery failures are c

ontained and never reach the agent loop.
- **Native on both desktop platforms.** macOS Notification
Center through a signed helper, `terminal-notifier`, `alerter` or `osascript`; Windows Action Center

through a WinRT toast posted by the bundled PowerShell helper.
- **Platform-aware by construction.*
* Only the channel matching the running `process.platform` is ever registered, so one profile config

uration works on macOS and Windows and the other platform's tooling is never spawned.
- **Five trigg
er families, live-editable.** Approvals, pending questions, long turns and background jobs, errors a
nd tool failures, and completions are each switchable in the settings card, with thresholds, reminde

rs and quiet hours.
- **Calm by default.** Dedupe keys, a per-session error cooldown, quiet hours wi

th urgent bypass, per-channel retry, and a circuit breaker.
- **Extensible.** Other plugins can post
notifications and register their own delivery channels through `ctx.notix`.

Every notification passes the same pipeline: quiet hours → dedupe → error cooldown → localized rende
ring → per-channel delivery. Dedupe keys are trigger-scoped and retained for 24 hours, so a repeated
event does not re-notify; error notifications within `triggers.error.cooldownMs` are suppressed per
session. Up to 200 notification records are kept in the `notix` storage domain (in memory when the
Host provides no storage domain) and are readable through `ctx.notix.history()`. Notifications suppr
essed by quiet hours, dedupe or cooldown are not recorded.
## What notifications look like
## Security and privacy
- **Never participates in decisions.** Notix does not register an approval answerer, so approvals ke

ep their fail-closed semantics; all decisions stay in the GUI.
- **Never touches the session log.**
It only observes events and projections; it never appends session events, and delivery failures cann

ot block or fail the agent.
- **Minimal content by default.** Notification text only contains the se
ssion title, tool name, and a truncated question or reason (questions at 160 characters; rendered ti
tles at most 120 and bodies at most 500). `verbosity: normal` adds a truncated error message (up to

200 characters). Command lines and file contents are never included.
- **Local only.** No network ca
lls: delivery spawns local OS tools (`osascript`, `terminal-notifier`, `alerter`, `powershell.exe`).
- **Contained failures.** Retries and a per-channel circuit breaker keep a broken backend from affe

cting the agent or other channels.
- **Local state.** Dedupe keys and notification history live in t
he Host's `notix` storage domain when one is available. The Windows channel writes only the per-user
AppUserModelId key (`DisplayName` and `IconUri`) and the macOS helper is an ordinary app bundle in
ey (`DisplayName` and `IconUri`) and the macOS helper is an ordinary app bundle in `~/Applications`.
